title: Use Supabase
summary: Supabase, file storage, security, backups and choosing services.

lessons.title: 1. Where does everything go?
lessons.concept: Code, data and files have different roles.

explanation.text: GitHub stores code and its history. Vercel builds and runs the site and API routes. Supabase Postgres stores rows: products, orders and profiles. Supabase Storage stores files: photos and documents. The database keeps the file path, not necessarily its contents. Browser storage is not your shop’s central backup.

The file library shows a private code snapshot from deployment time. It is neither a SQL console nor a database backup. Adding a project file does not automatically create a table. SQL changes are versioned in supabase/migrations and applied separately to the intended database.

lessons.title: 2. Create and connect a database
lessons.concept: A Supabase project is a space containing your database and its services.

explanation.text: For practice, create a Supabase project separate from the shop. Choose a region near your backend, keep the password in a password manager and open SQL Editor. In Settings → API Keys, locate the project URL and keys. Set the variables expected by your code in .env.local; restart your local server after changes.

A table groups one kind of object; a row represents one object; a column describes a property. Use primary keys, types, constraints and relationships. For money, prefer integer minor units or an appropriate numeric type. For orders, calculate prices and stock on the server and use a transaction for changes that must succeed together.

lessons.title: 3. Your first protected table
lessons.concept: RLS decides which rows a user can read or create.

explanation.text: Run this exercise once in the test project: this table stores notes owned by a Supabase Auth user. Signed-in users can read and create only their own notes. RLS filters rows; GRANT allows the operation type. This example grants no update or delete permission.

Test with two separate accounts through the client and with a signed-out user: B must not read A’s notes. SQL Editor or service_role tests do not prove that RLS protects clients. In a real app, also verify the server session and ownership of each resource; hiding a button does not protect a route.

lessons.title: 4. Store images and documents
lessons.concept: A bucket is a storage container with access rules.

explanation.text: In Supabase → Storage, create a test bucket. Public suits product photos meant for everyone; private suits customer documents. Set MIME types and a maximum size. Add policies on storage.objects: who may upload, read and delete? A public bucket makes reads public, not unrestricted writes.

After authentication, upload with the SDK or a signed upload URL, then save its path in a table. To read a private document, check access and generate a short-lived signed URL. Validate the actual content on the server too. Avoid keeping user files on a Vercel function’s disk: it is not durable storage.

lessons.title: 5. Backups, migrations and performance
lessons.concept: A migration changes structure; a backup lets you restore data.

explanation.text: Version SQL, test migrations on a test database, back up before a major change and verify data afterward. Rolling back a Vercel deployment does not undo SQL migrations. Prefer changes compatible with both old and new app versions during the transition.

Check backup retention and restore options in your plan. Supabase database backups do not contain Storage file binaries: back them up separately and test a restore. Index filtered columns, select only needed fields, paginate lists and monitor slow queries, errors, space and transfer costs.

lessons.title: 6. Which provider should you choose?
lessons.concept: Choose services based on your project’s actual needs.

explanation.text: My choice for L’ecomax: keep Supabase + Vercel + GitHub. Your site already uses this combination; it avoids a migration and covers relational data, file storage and code deployment. This is project-specific advice: no service is best for every need.

Supabase suits related data such as products and orders; learn SQL and RLS. Firebase/Firestore is worth considering for document-based apps with sync and offline support; study the data model and usage billing. Render suits a standalone Express, Django or FastAPI backend; you manage more server configuration.

Before choosing: compare region, data export, backups, support, quotas, read/write costs and outgoing traffic. Check current pricing and enable budget alerts. Start with a test project; a free plan is not a capacity or backup guarantee for a real shop.
